From cc71d37fd1f11e0495b1cf580909ebea37eaa886 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Feb 2022 17:18:58 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] HID: vivaldi: fix sysfs attributes leak

The driver creates the top row map sysfs attribute in input_configured()
method; unfortunately we do not have a callback that is executed when HID
interface is unbound, thus we are leaking these sysfs attributes, for
example when device is disconnected.

To fix it let's switch to managed version of adding sysfs attributes which
will ensure that they are destroyed when the driver is unbound.

Fixes: 14c9c014babe ("HID: add vivaldi HID driver")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>

diff --git a/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c b/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
index efa6140915f4..42ceb2058a09 100644
--- a/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
+++ b/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
@@ -144,7 +144,7 @@ static void vivaldi_feature_mapping(struct hid_device *hdev,
 static int vivaldi_input_configured(struct hid_device *hdev,
 				    struct hid_input *hidinput)
 {
-	return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
+	return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
 }
 
 static const struct hid_device_id vivaldi_table[] = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c`**
   - The function `vivaldi_input_configured` was modified to replace the call to `sysfs_create_group` with `devm_device_add_group`. This change ensures that the sysfs attributes created for the HID device are managed automatically, meaning they will be cleaned up when the device is unbound, preventing memory leaks.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `vivaldi_input_configured` directly addresses the issue of sysfs attribute leakage when the HID interface is unbound. By switching to a managed version of adding sysfs attributes, the patch ensures that the attributes are properly destroyed when the device is disconnected, thus fixing the bug identified in the original implementation. This change is a response to the lack of a callback for unbinding the HID interface, which was leading to the leak.

Here is the commit message:
HID: vivaldi: fix sysfs attributes leak

The driver creates the top row map sysfs attribute in input_configured()
method; unfortunately we do not have a callback that is executed when HID
interface is unbound, thus we are leaking these sysfs attributes, for
example when device is disconnected.

To fix it let's switch to managed version of adding sysfs attributes which
will ensure that they are destroyed when the driver is unbound.

Fixes: 14c9c014babe ("HID: add vivaldi HID driver")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the absence of a callback that is executed when the HID interface is unbound, leading to a situation where sysfs attributes created in the `input_configured` method remain allocated even after the device is disconnected, resulting in a memory leak.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int vivaldi_input_configured(struct hid_device *hdev,
 				    struct hid_input *hidinput)
 {
-	return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
+	return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
```
Reason:
The `sysfs_create_group` function creates sysfs attributes for the HID device, but there is no corresponding cleanup mechanism when the device is unbound. This results in the sysfs attributes remaining allocated even after the device is disconnected, causing a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
```
Reason:
The `devm_device_add_group` function manages the lifecycle of the sysfs attributes automatically. It ensures that the attributes are destroyed when the driver is unbound, thus preventing the memory leak that occurs when the device is disconnected.
